content:
iPadOS and macOS were once two distinctly different software platforms. But since iPadOS 26, they have become increasingly similar. This year it's even more apparent — iPadOS 27 adds three features that bring the iPad closer to the Mac.

#1: Status bar shows app name

I spend nearly all my time using an M5 iPad Pro connected to a Magic Keyboard. For keyboard users, there's always been one problem with the iPad — the lack of a clear "current app" indicator.

If only one app is on screen, it's not an issue. But when several apps are open at once, keyboard shortcuts become easy to press incorrectly. I've lost count of how many times I expected a shortcut to trigger within one app, only for it to execute in another.

Mac solved this problem long ago, displaying the current app's name in the top-left corner of the screen. Now iPadOS 27 can do the same.

iPadOS 27 users will see the current app's name in the status bar, displayed alongside status bar elements like time and date. It's not a massive change, but using the iPad with a keyboard is noticeably more comfortable.

#2: Permanently visible menu bar

Another welcome change in iPadOS 27 is the ability to set the menu bar to remain permanently visible.

Apple first brought the menu bar to the iPad last year. But unlike on the Mac, the iPadOS 26 menu bar only appeared when the user actively summoned it.

In iPadOS 27's Settings, under "Multitasking & Gestures," a new option has appeared, labelled "Auto-show and hide menu bar."

Simply turn this option off and the menu bar will remain visible at all times. I've been using it this way during the iPadOS beta — it's one of my favourite changes this year.

#3: Everyday operation speeds more Mac-like

Although I really love my iPad and I'm grateful for the new features brought by iPadOS 26 and 27, sometimes I still get frustrated by how slow some basic operations are. As I wrote earlier this year: "Right-click menus in iPadOS often feel sluggish and laggy, but on the Mac they're instant."

Fortunately, Apple has been actively working to close this gap this year, and I'm happy to say that iPadOS 27 does bring substantial improvements to the speed of these everyday operations.

Apple says right-click menus open faster when using a cursor, and I can definitely feel it myself. Browsing files and transferring them to an external hard drive is "up to 5x faster" — Apple says it's now as quick as Finder on the Mac. App launches are more responsive, and window management for minimising, switching or dragging windows is smoother.

There are still some areas where the Mac is faster than the iPad, and the iPad can feel a little sluggish. But overall, the speed improvements in iPadOS 27 are a big step in the right direction.

Which new features and changes in iPadOS 27 suit you best? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
